# Code of Conduct

## Purpose

This repository supports teaching, learning, and academic collaboration. Everyone who participates is expected to help maintain a respectful, inclusive, constructive, and academically responsible environment.

This Code of Conduct applies to students, faculty, staff, maintainers, contributors, and visitors.

## Expected Behavior

Participants are expected to:

* Communicate respectfully and professionally.
* Welcome people with different backgrounds, identities, abilities, perspectives, and levels of technical experience.
* Critique ideas, code, and processes rather than individuals.
* Give and receive constructive feedback with patience and good faith.
* Provide enough context for others to understand questions, problems, and proposed changes.
* Respect reasonable boundaries and requests to end an interaction.
* Protect personal, academic, institutional, and security-sensitive information.
* Credit sources and contributions appropriately.
* Follow course instructions and applicable academic-integrity requirements.
* Use artificial intelligence and other assistance tools only as permitted by the course and disclose or cite their use when required.
* Accept responsibility for mistakes and take reasonable steps to correct any resulting harm.

## Unacceptable Behavior

The following behavior is not acceptable:

* Harassment, intimidation, discrimination, stalking, or threats.
* Insults, personal attacks, ridicule, trolling, or deliberately inflammatory comments.
* Unwelcome sexual attention or sexualized language, images, or conduct.
* Publishing another person’s private information without permission.
* Posting grades, private instructor feedback, student identification numbers, access credentials, private communications, or other sensitive information.
* Impersonating another person or misrepresenting someone’s identity, work, or contributions.
* Repeatedly disrupting discussions, submitting spam, or continuing off-topic task after being asked to stop.
* Sharing, requesting, or publishing completed coursework in a manner that violates course instructions or academic-integrity requirements.
* Presenting another person’s work as one’s own or helping another person misrepresent authorship.
* Conducting unauthorized security testing or posting malicious code, credentials, exploits, or instructions intended to cause harm.
* Attempting to evade moderation or enforcement actions.
* Retaliating against someone who reports a concern or participates in its review.
* Other conduct that would reasonably interfere with a safe, respectful, and productive academic environment.

## Academic Integrity

This Code of Conduct complements, but does not replace, course requirements or institutional academic-integrity policies.

Permitted collaboration, reuse, citation, and use of artificial intelligence may vary by course or assignment. Participants who are uncertain about what is allowed should ask the course instructor through an approved course communication channel before proceeding.

Potential academic-integrity violations should not be investigated or debated publicly in repository issues, pull requests, or discussions.

## Privacy and Security

Do not post sensitive information in public or shared repository spaces. Before posting screenshots, logs, files, or links, remove information such as:

* Full names when they are not necessary
* Student identification numbers
* Grades or private feedback
* Email addresses and other contact information
* Passwords, tokens, keys, and authentication details
* Private repository URLs or access information
* Personal, educational, or institutional records

If sensitive information is posted accidentally, remove it when possible and notify an appropriate repository maintainer or institutional contact promptly.

## Scope

This Code of Conduct applies to participation in repository-related spaces, including:

* Issues and issue comments
* Discussions and replies
* Pull requests and code reviews
* Commit messages and comments
* Wikis and other repository documentation
* Repository-linked communication or collaboration spaces
* Interactions in which someone is officially representing the repository or course community

Applicable institutional policies, course requirements, and the [GitHub Terms of Service and Community Guidelines](https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy) also apply. When requirements differ, participants must follow the requirement with authority over the particular course, institution, or platform.

## Reporting a Concern

Do not report sensitive conduct concerns in a public issue or discussion.

Use the most appropriate private channel:

1. Contact the course instructor through the institution’s approved private communication method.
2. If the concern involves the instructor or cannot be addressed at the course level, use the institution’s established reporting, student-support, or conduct process.
3. Report task that may violate GitHub’s policies through [GitHub Support](https://support.github.com/).

Repository support options may also be listed in [SUPPORT.md](SUPPORT.md).

Include only the information needed to understand the concern, such as the relevant repository location, date, participants, and a factual description of what occurred. Do not redistribute sensitive material more broadly than necessary.

Reports will be handled as privately as reasonably possible, consistent with applicable institutional policies, legal obligations, and the need to investigate and respond.

## Moderation and Enforcement

Repository maintainers may take reasonable actions to protect the community and preserve productive use of the repository. Depending on the circumstances, these actions may include:

* Clarifying expectations
* Requesting that content or behavior be corrected
* Editing, hiding, or removing inappropriate content
* Locking or limiting a conversation
* Restricting repository participation
* Blocking or reporting an account
* Referring a concern through applicable institutional processes

Responses will consider the context, severity, impact, and pattern of behavior. Serious conduct may be referred immediately without first using less restrictive measures.

Any academic, employment, or institutional disciplinary consequences will be determined through the applicable course and institutional processes, not solely through repository moderation.

## Questions

Questions about repository participation should be directed through the support channels identified in [SUPPORT.md](SUPPORT.md). Questions about course requirements, collaboration, or academic integrity should be directed privately to the course instructor.

## Provisional Status

Formal institutional review and approval of this Code of Conduct are pending. This interim document may be revised or replaced after that review is complete.

This Code of Conduct does not replace or modify applicable institutional policies, course requirements, contractual obligations, laws, or platform terms. If a conflict exists, the controlling institutional policy, course requirement, law, or platform term takes precedence.

* [GitHub Community Guidelines](https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/github-terms/github-community-guidelines?utm_source=chatgpt.com), including its expectations for respectful participation, moderation, and reporting.
* [GitHub Terms of Service](https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/github-terms/github-terms-of-service), which governs participation and content hosted on GitHub.
* [Adding a Code of Conduct to Your Project](https://docs.github.com/en/communities/setting-up-your-project-for-healthy-contributions/adding-a-code-of-conduct-to-your-project), which provides GitHub’s implementation guidance for repository codes of conduct.
* Applicable institutional conduct, academic-integrity, privacy, accessibility, and acceptable-use policies.
